newsitem.title: NIGERIA: NIGERIA BUDGET CRISIS CUTS ELF DRILLING.
newsitem.headline: NIGERIA BUDGET CRISIS CUTS ELF DRILLING.

text.p: Budget cuts by Nigeria's military government have forced Elf-Aquitaine's local joint-venture to scale back its plan for exploratory drilling in 1997, the company's exploration manager said.

"Earlier on we programmed a good number of wells for this year but now we have the possibility of drilling only one well in the joint venture operations," Chwuemeka Ikelionwu said in an interview with Elf's in-house magazine, which Reuters received on Wednesday.
Nigeria's joint venture partners have complained that they have been forced to cut back on new projects after an across the board cut to $2.05 billion from a proposed $3.32 billion budget for 1997.
"The budget cut hit exploration below the belt, normally the cut is on new programmes which in most cases affects exploration more," Ikelionwu said.
A meeting between the oil companies and senior government officials to discuss the funding crisis was put off for a second time on Tuesday and no new date has yet been set.
Ikelionwu said Elf would go ahead with drilling three deep offshore wells, programmed under its Production Sharing Contract, which are not reliant on the government for funding.
"We have drilled two, the third will be drilled before the year runs out," he said.
